subject: outage
text: 2026-08-26 outage, root-caused from the operator's screenshot: the bootstrap died at the OPTIONAL browser install (his PC has Python 3.9 + pip 21, playwright's greenlet fell back to an MSVC source build and failed) and the script threw - so the REQUIRED Core never started and the wall showed connection refused. Two design faults, both fixed: (1) bootstrap now requires Python 3.10+, installs 3.12 via winget when absent, upgrades pip, installs optional deps wheels-only, and a browser-install failure WARNS and continues - optional steps can never again kill the required path; browse tests skip honestly when playwright is absent; aletheia/__init__ refuses pre-3.10 Python with words instead of syntax errors. (2) Found while tracing: a Core started without the supervisor would exit on the next code merge leaving nothing listening - now a supervised Core (env marker) exits 42 for its supervisor, an unsupervised one hands off to a detached supervisor instead of orphaning the port; supervisor install starts the task immediately; a second supervisor yields when a Core already answers.

subject: outage
text: Second failure from the operator's rerun screenshot: his clone had locally journaled lines from the old Core, git pull --ff-only aborted on them, and the bootstrap continued on STALE code (PowerShell does not stop on native exit codes). Root disease fixed, not the symptom: (1) per-writer journal files - the cloud writes journal.jsonl, the PC Core writes journal-pc.jsonl (journal.use_pc_journal at Core/supervisor start), entries() merges all writer files into one time-ordered stream, so journal git conflicts are structurally impossible; (2) core_tick commits local state BEFORE pulling so rebases always run on a clean tree, and pushes every tick so checkpoints publish without waiting for a receipt; autostash-conflict output is now detected as failure; (3) bootstrap is a true recovery tool - fetch, salvage local journal lines into journal-pc.jsonl, hard reset to origin/main, exit-code checks on every git step with clear messages.

subject: outage
text: Third failed run, root cause CallDepthOverflow: the bootstrap helper 'function Py' shadowed py.exe (PowerShell resolves function names before applications), so it recursed until the session died at the required checks. Also he caught the ten-minute window between PR23 and PR24, so the repo-healing wasn't in his script. Fixes: no wrapper functions at all - the interpreter resolves once to its .exe path (Get-Command -CommandType Application) and every call checks LASTEXITCODE explicitly; Remove-Item function:Py at script top so a stale function from an old run in the same window can't shadow anything; salvage now writes journal-pc.jsonl via .NET UTF8 no-BOM (Add-Content -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM in Windows PowerShell that would corrupt the first JSON line) and journal reads utf-8-sig; and after auto-start the script now WAITS for /api/status before opening the wall, so the operator never sees connection-refused again during setup.

subject: defect
text: OPERATOR-REPORTED DEFECT 2026-08-27, fixed: black console windows titled 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe' popping up on the PC desktop every 60 seconds. Cause: my sync loop shells out to git ~1440x/day, and under the supervisor's hidden logon task the parent is pythonw.exe which has NO console - so Windows gave every short-lived child its own console window. He asked what had infected his computer, which is the correct reaction to ambient software behaving like malware. Fixed as a CLASS not an instance: new aletheia/proc.py adds CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows, and every bookkeeping subprocess routes through it (sync.py git, supervisor.py schtasks+powershell, voice_room.py TTS powershell, pulse.py git log). tests/test_proc.py statically parses those modules and fails on any raw subprocess.run without an explicit '# proc: visible-by-design' comment stating why the operator should see that window - the Core relaunch is the one documented exception, because from start-aletheia.bat he deliberately opened a window to watch it. LESSON: no test could have caught this; it took a human looking at his own desktop. Ambient software must be judged on how it FEELS to live with, not only on whether it passes.

subject: review:standing-grants
text: CATCH-UP REVIEW FINDING, repaired: all three standing grants (work_trust, secret_trust, code_trust) could be manufactured remotely. active() validated (a) a grant file under state/private/ - gitignored, but .gitignore only stops an ACCIDENTAL add, not 'git add -f' - and (b) policy.is_approved(), whose approvals live in state/approvals/ and are ALREADY tracked and public. Both factors travel over the Core's sync pull, and nothing bound either to the machine. One push could have minted standing workstation trust, secret-fill authority, or autonomous-PR authority on the PC. Only the working agreement about who writes what stood in the way, and that is not a gate. FIX: aletheia/machine_binding.py - HMAC over each grant's identity/approval/expiry/limits, keyed by a 32-byte secret created on first use in ~/.aletheia/machine.key, outside the repo. enable() mints it; active() refuses without it. 12 regression tests prove a grant minted elsewhere is inert even with a valid approval, and that tampering with limits/expiry/approval breaks the signature. Existing grants on the PC fail closed and say so once via notification + journal with the one command to restore.

subject: review:code-loop-authority
text: CATCH-UP REVIEW, Priority 3 findings repaired. (1) PROTECTED PATHS INCOMPLETE - the autonomous code worker could propose edits to config/ (fleet front-door grants AND every capability's approval_policy), to CLAUDE.md and docs/PLAYBOOK.md (the rules it is judged by), and to authority modules machine_binding/work_direct/sealed_observe/github_auth/core/supervisor/sync/portfolio/project_autostart. CLAUDE.md says authority widens only by a reviewed registry edit, never a code path around the check - an unattended worker opening PRs against the registries IS such a path even though a human merges, because the loop's premise is running while nobody watches. Extended PROTECTED_PREFIXES with config/ and .claude/, added the authority modules and governance docs to ALETHEIA_PROTECTED. (2) PATH NORMALIZATION BYPASS, found by the new test: _safe_path returned the RAW string while PurePosixPath silently folds a leading './', so './config/fleet.json' passed the traversal checks and then failed to match the 'config/' prefix - the registries were reachable through that spelling. It now returns the normalized path. (3) CHATGPT BROWSER LEASE WAS INHERITABLE - #74 made browser reasoning require ALETHEIA_ALLOW_CHATGPT_BROWSER_REASONING=1, but env vars are inherited: starting the Core or supervisor from a leased shell handed every always-on loop the right to open his signed-in ChatGPT. Added browser_reasoner.drop_lease(), called in core.main() at startup and in supervisor._child_env(), so the always-on side actively drops what it inherited rather than merely declining to set it. RATIFIED as sound: work_direct's quote-sha256 plan binding plus its public-bus allowlist and the underlying work_session classifier; secret_store taking values only via getpass so plaintext never reaches argv, shell history or process listings.

subject: review:pr76-pr75
text: PR #76 (guarantee eventual follow-up delivery) RATIFIED and merged into the reviewed tree - it applies cleanly to CURRENT main, not just its old base. Design is right: the durable delivery record is committed BEFORE the notification is published (write-ahead ordering, so a crash between them loses nothing), an answer interrupted by a Core restart becomes an explicit FAILED with recovered_after_restart rather than pretending it is still thinking, terminal replies stay IMPORTANT until the requesting surface actually takes them, and durable=True is opt-in rather than a behaviour change everywhere. PR #75 SUPERSEDED except for one genuinely unique piece, now ported: _attention_say() answers 'what needs my attention' from durable local queues instead of a ~90-second planner round trip - the fastest answer AND the most honest one, since it reports what the stores contain with nothing to invent. Everything else in #75 (collection window, transient retry, deferral) is covered more completely by #76. 1251 tests green.
